text:
sara: Heads-up — after enabling prefetch sampling on the collector we started seeing exporter CPU p99 spikes and a few customer-facing timeouts. Anyone else seeing this?

mike: which exporter + config? stack or otlp?

sara: OTLP grpc exporter to s3-archiver cluster. Sample config change was: `sampling.prefetch: true`, `sampling.rate: 0.2`, `exporter.batch_size: 512`, `exporter.threads: 6`

ben: 512 batch + prefetch can blow up CPU if span volume is high. Prefetch increases memory + serialization pressure. p99 CPU makes sense.

jess: do we have graphs? per-route span-insert rate and exporter CPU over same window?

sara: attaching quick paste from console logs (trimmed):
```
2024-11-02T14:12:03Z exporter_worker[3] serialize_ms=22 payload_bytes=1048576 spans=480
2024-11-02T14:12:04Z exporter_worker[2] serialize_ms=85 payload_bytes=2097152 spans=1024
2024-11-02T14:12:05Z exporter_worker[5] export_err=0 retry=0
```

mike: those serialize_ms spikes are red flags. Are we compressing payloads? gzip adds CPU.

sara: yes gzip=true on that route. We turned gzip on for network cost.

ben: combos that kill CPU: large batch_size + gzip + prefetch + many small spans. One option: reduce batch_size and enable batching window to 50ms. Or consider disabling gzip for high-throughput routes.

jess: tradeoff: disabling gzip raises egress cost. But we should protect p99 and SLAs. Maybe route-level quotas to cap spans/sec per key?

mike: we discussed a quota shim in routing policy earlier. Can we do fast drop for noisy routes before serialize stage? lightweight token-bucket per-route in collector.

ben: yes token-bucket upstream is cheap. Also sampler should reduce span count earlier. Current prefetch sampler runs post-ingest which keeps full KV cache -> cost. Move sampling earlier to the socket read is ideal.

sara: moving earlier would help but will remove spans from traces we might need for debugging. jess might veto. :grimacing:

jess: we need a middle ground: adaptive sampling + per-route preserve-set for error traces. Keep all spans for routes flagged `preserve=true` in routing config.

mike: console UX ask: can we expose a per-route throttle toggle and a quick preview of expected token + cost impact? Product asked yesterday.

ben: the backend pieces: 1) route token-bucket 2) early sampler switch 3) exporter batch/window tuning 4) per-route gzip override. Any one helps.

alert-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: exporter_cpu.p99 > 90th percentile for 3m on cluster s3-archiver (alert_id: 2024-11-02/exp-503)

sara: ok let's do short-term mitigations: reduce batch_size=256 and set exporter.threads=4 for that cluster, disable gzip for the noisy tenant. Can infra flip that config quickly?

mike: I can patch the hot-config tomorrow morning, but we should do a canary first. I'll push to canary region 1 now.

ben: also rolling a quick sampler change: `sampling.rate` -> 0.1 for that tenant and enable `preserve_on_error=true` so we keep errors.

jess: +1. Please add a console flag to mark a tenant as `preserve` so support can flip it without eng intervention. UX: a 2-state toggle with tooltip explaining fidelity vs cost.

sara: noted. I'll file a product ticket. For telemetry graphs, can someone add an overlay of exporter.serialize_ms vs spans/sec in the route dashboard? Helps Correlate.

mike: will add the overlay and a vertical line for the config change.

ben: long-term: let's prototype an early sampler at the socket layer and a cheap route-level dropper in collector. That should keep exporter CPU bounded.

jess: agree. Also add automated regression alerting in the console: if exporter CPU p99 rises 30% after a rollout, auto-fallback.

sara: thanks all. I'll update this thread after canary results. :thumbsup:
